title: Console: show active runtime hardware profile + profile version in debugging views (minimal UI spec)
creator: Talia Benson
project: Hardware tuning profiles pack (Serving Runtime Performance — Kernel + Scheduling)
description:
Context
- Runtime is rolling out a versioned “hardware tuning profile pack” (H100/B200/L40S) with deterministic selection + guardrails.
- On-call and customer-facing teams need to quickly answer: “What profile is active right now?” and “What version is it?” when investigating perf regressions, OOMs, or kernel fallbacks.
- This ticket defines a minimal Console/ops UX spec to surface the active profile in the most-used debugging views, without expanding scope into full profile management UI.

Goal
- In Redwood Console, surface the effective runtime hardware profile identifiers:
  1) active profile_id (e.g., h100-default, l40s-stable)
  2) active profile_version (e.g., 1.22.0)
  3) detected hardware sku (H100 / L40S / B200) as a sanity check
- Make it easy to copy/paste these values into Slack/Linear/Jira and correlate with dashboards/metrics.

Non-goals
- Building a “profile editor” or per-knob override UI.
- Exposing low-level kernel variant strings or internal tuning knobs directly to customers.
- Building new permissions/RBAC systems (work within existing Console visibility tiers).

Primary users
- SRE/on-call (Hosted canary + broad rollout triage)
- Runtime engineers (perf regression debugging)
- Dedicated support / Solutions Engineering (customer escalations; profile pin/rollback discussions)

Data sources / definitions (align with Runtime)
- Effective values to display should come from the runtime (not control-plane intent):
  - profile_id (string)
  - profile_version (string)
  - sku (string)
- Secondary (optional, if already available with low effort):
  - “Pinned profile version” (customer override) vs “Effective profile version” (what runtime is running)
  - “Profile source” (fleet default vs customer pin) — only if Runtime already emits a safe, stable enum.

Placement (minimal UI)
1) Deployment / Pool detail page (Dedicated + Hosted internal)
- Add a small “Runtime profile” block near other runtime metadata (e.g., runtime version, region).
- Fields:
  - Hardware SKU: <H100|L40S|B200>
  - Active profile: <profile_id>
  - Profile version: <profile_version>
- Interaction:
  - Copy-to-clipboard icon on each value.
  - Link “View dashboard” → points to the “Runtime Profiles” dashboard filtered by sku + profile_id (if a stable URL pattern exists; otherwise omit link).

2) Request / Trace / Debug event view (where we already show route/model/region)
- Add a single-line chip row entry:
  - “Profile: <profile_id> (<profile_version>) · SKU: <sku>”
- This is to reduce back-and-forth during incident triage when a trace is shared.

3) Support bundle / debug export (if the UI already supports exporting a ‘debug bundle’)
- Ensure active profile_id + profile_version + sku are included in the exported metadata section.
- If support bundle UI is out of scope, at least document the intended strings so Support can request it in ENG.

Copy + formatting
- Use exact key names consistent with runtime tags where possible:
  - profile_id
  - profile_version
  - sku
- Display format (recommended):
  - Active profile: h100-default
  - Profile version: 1.22.0
  - Hardware SKU: H100
- If a value is unavailable: show “Unknown” with a tooltip: “Runtime did not report a profile value for this instance.”

Visibility / permissions
- Hosted: internal-only Console views may show more detail; external customer Console should show only the safe trio (sku/profile_id/profile_version).
- Dedicated: customer admins can see these fields because they map directly to performance expectations and troubleshooting, but avoid showing kernel-level details.
- Private: if Console connects to private control plane, same external rules apply.

Edge cases
- Mixed pools / rolling restarts:
  - If the page aggregates multiple instances, show:
    - “Active profile (majority): …” + “Variance detected” badge
    - Variance popover: list top 2–3 combinations with percentage counts (only if telemetry provides it). If not available, don’t invent; show instance-level in a table.
- Profile mismatch during model reload:
  - If runtime reports profile changes over time, show “Last updated at <timestamp>” (only if we have it already).

Acceptance criteria
- Console surfaces profile_id + profile_version + sku in at least ONE high-traffic debugging page used by on-call (deployment/pool OR trace view).
- Values are copyable.
- Labels/copy reviewed with Runtime (Noah) and SRE (Sean) to ensure terminology matches incident workflow.
- Confirm fields are safe to expose to Dedicated customers (Product sign-off: Lauren).

Open questions (to resolve during review)
1) Which Console page is the best minimal insertion point for launch: Deployment/Pool details vs Trace view?
2) Is “profile_version pin” vs “effective profile_version” available in API/telemetry already, or do we only show effective runtime values?
3) Do we have a stable dashboard deep link pattern for filtering by profile_id/sku?

Design deliverables
- Minimal UI spec with:
  - placement + component notes
  - exact strings/labels
  - empty/unknown state
  - screenshot-level annotation (can be a lightweight mock)
- If a Figma is created, attach link here.

References
- Epic: ENG-4921 (Hardware tuning profiles pack)
- Observability tagging: ENG-4931 (tags for profile_id, sku)
- Runtime debug endpoint addition: PR-25014 (profile pack version in /health + debug)
- Dashboard work: observability-pack/pr-221 (“Runtime Profiles” overview)
comments: 2026-01-16 — Talia Benson: Creating this as a minimal design task so we don’t block runtime-1.22 on full UI polish. Key requirement is copy/pasteable profile_id + profile_version + sku in at least one place in Console that on-call uses.

2026-01-22 — Allison Grant: From dashboards POV, having profile_id and sku visible in Console will reduce back-and-forth when someone is trying to align a customer report with the ‘Runtime Profiles’ dashboard panels. Deep link is nice-to-have; we can provide a generic dashboard link initially.

2026-02-03 — Sean Gallagher: During incident triage we mostly live in trace view + deployment/pool page. If we only pick one, please pick trace view. We frequently paste trace links into Slack and need the profile info right there.

2026-02-06 — Lauren Bishop: Customer-facing Console can show these fields (profile/version/sku) as long as we avoid surfacing internal kernel variant names. Please label as ‘Active profile’ not ‘Tuning preset’—customers have already heard ‘profile’ in comms draft.

2026-02-12 — Noah Patel: Runtime can emit effective profile_id/profile_version/sku reliably. Pinned vs effective is available in control-plane but not yet unified in one API response; recommend shipping only effective in v1 to avoid confusing mismatches.

2026-02-20 — Talia Benson: Marking In Review. Proposal: implement in Trace view first with a single-line chip: ‘Profile: <id> (<version>) · SKU: <sku>’ plus copy icon. Deployment page can follow as a second iteration if time permits.
